methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $60M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
TS Conductor is a Series B climate and energy company that has raised $60M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 private companies and 1 public peer (Linaçor, ticker LNZA) operating in the same sector and stage, including KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, Amogy, and Redwood Materials.

Two valuation methods were applied. The stage-progression method uses the company's $60M total raised as a proxy baseline and applies a 1.9x multiplier typical for Series B-to-next-stage advancement, yielding $114M. The peer-median approach references three same-sector, adjacent-stage comparables: KoBold Metals at $3.0B (Series C), Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B (Series C), and Amogy at $700M (Series C). The median valuation across these three peers is $1.0B, with a range of $700M to $3.0B.

The two methods produce a triangulated valuation range of $97M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $557M. The substantial spread reflects key uncertainties: the stage-progression method relies on raised capital as a proxy for intrinsic value, while the peer-median approach incorporates more mature Series C companies, suggesting considerable variance in how markets have valued climate-tech enterprises at adjacent stages. Critical drivers include the company's technology differentiation relative to the peer set and near-term commercialization milestones.
